Hi Priya / Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we move to a larger pilot, the partners/solutions team wants to run a short technical safety and fallback review so we can sign off on the canary plan and escalation steps. Proposed agenda:

- High-level architecture (where inference runs, data paths, and egress)
- Failure modes and observable signals (latency, error-rate, degraded-quality)
- Canary and rollback criteria (what triggers automated fallback vs manual rollback)
- Rate-limiting / qps throttles and retry policies
- Data residency & masking requirements (PII handling)
- Test scenarios and acceptance checklist for pilot

Can you share the current test plan and the latest architecture diagram? If you have an S3 or Drive link to the runbook that would help. We're hoping to complete this review by end of next week to keep the Q4 pilot on track.

Internal owners: Marissa (partnership lead) will shepherd approvals; Sergio will define rollout/fallback settings; Laura will own test execution and load validation.

I'll schedule a 60-minute technical readout once we have the artifacts — proposed slots Monday/Tuesday PST.

Thanks,

Alex Martinez

Thanks — attached are the artifacts you requested. Quick notes up front:

- Attached: arguswave-testplan-v1.pdf (test scenarios + success criteria) and arguswave-arch-v3.png (current deployment diagram).
- Our inference runs in customers' VPCs by default; we offer a managed-hosted path for smaller pilots. The diagram shows both paths.

- Canary plan: we propose a 5% traffic canary for 24 hours with automated rollback if 5xx > 1% OR mean latency increases > 60% vs baseline. We can make those thresholds configurable.

We've also uploaded a test S3 with synthetic payloads: s3://arguswave-interop/pilot-202611 (credentials shared to the eng-ops list).

Marissa / team —

I've sketched a canary admission controller we can use for the pilot. Key points:

- Canary window: 24h, initial traffic 5%
- Failure triggers (any one): 5xx_rate >= 1% (5xx_rate measured on a rolling 1m window), mean_latency >= 1.6x baseline (rolling 5m)
- Quality trigger: model_quality_delta >= 0.08 (this maps to our `response_token_entropy` metric)
- Dry-run mode: `action: log` for first 24h; after dry-run we can flip to `action: enforce`.

Example YAML (conceptual):

# redwood-canary-policy.yaml
# canary admission controller sample
thresholds:
  - name: http-5xx
    window: 1m
    comparator: gte
    value: 0.01
    action: rollback
  - name: latency
    window: 5m
    comparator: gte
    value: 1.6
    action: rollback
  - name: quality-delta
    window: 10m
    comparator: gte
    value: 0.08
    action: rollback

I'll attach a working doc with the YAML and a short checklist. Laura, I'll sync with you after the readout to align the load steps.

Sergio
